subject: Stagewise wipe runbook and order form for bespoke residency windows
messages:
From: Jonah Blake <jonah.blake@helixcare.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixcare.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Bespoke residency windows + staged deletion request

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelixCare is close to finalizing the procurement worksheet but we have a specific ask around data residency and deletion that needs to be captured in the order form. Our legal team requires a stagewise (phased) deletion model for customer PII across the following buckets:

- Active workspace (retained indefinitely per customer setting)
- Short-term archive: purge 30 days after deactivation
- Long-term quarantine: encrypted hold for 12 months, then automated erase in 30-day rolling batches
- Emergency escrow: immediate snapshot retained for up to 90 days for incident investigation, removable on certified request

We need an explicit runbook and SLA language that defines who performs the wipe, the observable signals (audit logs/events), verification artifacts (signed deletion certificate), and timetables for each stage. Please see the attached HelixCare_stagewise-wipe_spec_request.pdf for format.

Two quick questions to help us draft the contract clause:
1) Can Redwood provide a Certificate of Deletion with ISO timestamp and HMAC of deleted dataset metadata?
2) For the long-term quarantine, can we confirm the erase process is irreversible and that snapshot copies (backups) are included in the 12-month timer?

We're aiming to execute the order form before EoQ (end of November). Would appreciate a runbook draft and a proposed order-form clause we can circulate to procurement/legal.

Best,
Jonah
Procurement Lead, HelixCare
procurement@helixcare.com

Attachment: HelixCare_stagewise-wipe_spec_request.pdf (application/pdf, 214KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jonah Blake <jonah.blake@helixcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Bespoke residency windows + staged deletion request

Hi Jonah — thanks for the clear spec and the attachment. We can support a stagewise wipe model; below is a concise plan we can convert into an order-form clause and an attached runbook.

High-level response to your questions:
1) Certificate of Deletion: yes — we can emit a signed Deletion Certificate including ISO8601 timestamp, a deletion event ID, list of affected object keys, and an HMAC over the metadata. The certificate will be signed with our KMS key and stored in the customer audit log for 7 years (or per your retention selection).
2) Backups and snapshots: we will include any customer snapshots and backup copies under the same 12-month quarantine timer by default. If you require extended backup retention exclusion, we can note that as an exception in the order form.

Proposed stage definitions (for order form):
- Active: retention controlled via customer setting. Not part of automated wipe.
- Short-term archive: automated purge 30 days after workspace deactivation; purge job runs nightly and produces a deletion certificate within 24 hours of completion.
- Long-term quarantine: encrypted hold for up to 12 months from deactivation, after which a two-stage erase occurs: (a) logical deletion + metadata HMAC and audit entries; (b) physical tokenized erase executed within 30 days.
- Emergency escrow: snapshot retained up to 90 days, explicit erase initiated on verified signed request; cert issued on completion.

Operational notes:
- Wipes will be executed by our Dedicated Data Lifecycle service (internal team) with runbook steps, playbooks for verification, and a post-action signed certificate.
- Customers will receive webhook events for each stage and a downloadable delete-certificate artifact.
- For SLA, we propose a 99.9% windowed completion target for Short-term archive (within 48 hours of scheduled purge) and a 30-day completion SLO for the physical phase of Long-term quarantine.

I'll draft an order-form clause and a runbook doc (orderform + runbook attachments) and loop in Marissa (AM) for procurement terms and Karthik/Markus for the technical/ops wording. Any specific wording your legal prefers for "irreversible" and "backup inclusion" would be helpful.

Thanks — will send the draft today.

—Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachment: stagewise-wipe-orderform-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 45KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Bespoke residency windows + staged deletion request — technical runbook notes

FYI — forwarding my quick notes for the runbook. I pulled the short list into inline bullets to make the order-form language precise.

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 09:12 Jonah Blake <jonah.blake@helixcare.com> wrote:
> Hi Sean,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week — HelixCare is close to finalizing the procurement worksheet but we have a specific ask around data residency and deletion that needs to be captured in the order form.
> (attached)

Karthik's runbook notes (for inclusion in the doc):
- Deletion Certificate: include fields: deletion_id, timestamp_iso, object_count, object_digest_list (max 1k entries per cert), signer_kms_key_id, cert_hmac.
- Backup handling: add explicit line "Backups and replicated snapshots are included in the deletion schedule unless an explicit backup-exclusion clause is added by HelixCare."
- Irreversibility phrasing: use "cryptographic irreversibility" and define it as zero-knowledge unrecoverability when keys are redacted; avoid absolute language like "forever unrecoverable" which legal dislikes.
- Testing and verification: a quarterly table-top wipe test can be scheduled; results produce a signed report.

Open items for legal/procurement:
- Does HelixCare require deletion certificates in PDF or machine-readable JSON? (we can support both)
- Are there specific backup services to exclude?

I'll pull this into the doc and hand to Markus for SLA targets and to Marissa for contract language.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Quoted original attachment: HelixCare_stagewise-wipe_spec_request.pdf)

From: Jonah Blake <jonah.blake@helixcare.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixcare.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Bespoke residency windows + staged deletion request

Sean / Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed notes. HelixCare legal reviewed Karthik's proposed phrasing and we're comfortable with the "cryptographic irreversibility" definition. A few small asks before we sign:

- Please include an explicit line in the order form that backups/snapshots are treated as "included by default" unless a named exclusion is requested.
- Deletion Certificate: PDF preferred for signature but we also want a machine-readable JSON artifact for audit ingestion.
- SLA buckets: we accept the 48-hour short-archive target and the 30-day physical phase SLO as long as the order form includes an exception process for emergency accelerations (procurement approvals via e-signed form).

If you can attach the final order form with those three edits and a DocuSign link, procurement can route for signatures today.

Thanks — Jonah
Procurement Lead, HelixCare
procurement@helixcare.com
